symptom: PC-A in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC-B in VLAN 10 connected to Switch 2.
ai_root_cause: Trunk port FastEthernet0/1 on Switch1 is configured to only allow VLAN 20 ('switchport trunk allowed vlan 20'), blocking VLAN 10 traffic across the trunk link.
ai_evidence: show_running_config_Switch1 shows interface FastEthernet0/1 with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan 20' and show_interfaces_trunk_Switch1 shows 'Vlans allowed on trunk 20'
ai_fix_steps: Enter Switch1 interface configuration mode: 'interface FastEthernet0/1'; Add VLAN 10 to the allowed trunk list: 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 10'; Verify trunk VLAN forwarding state: 'show interfaces trunk'

symptom: PC-1 in VLAN 20 is unable to obtain traffic or reach gateway. Switch logs report native VLAN mismatch.
ai_root_cause: Native VLAN mismatch on trunk link between Switch1 (VLAN 10) and Switch2 (VLAN 1).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Configure 'switchport trunk native vlan 10' on Switch2 interface GigabitEthernet0/1.

symptom: PC connected to Switch1 Fa0/5 has no network access and fails all pings.
ai_root_cause: Rule check failure: VLAN 30 assigned to Fa0/5 is missing from switch VLAN database.
ai_evidence: Deterministic Check [VLAN Database Check]: VLAN 30 assigned to Fa0/5 is missing from switch VLAN database.
ai_fix_steps: Create VLAN 30 on Switch1 using 'vlan 30' followed by 'name Admin'.

symptom: PC-2 attached to Fa0/10 cannot reach default gateway 192.168.1.1.
ai_root_cause: Switch port Fa0/10 is assigned to default VLAN 1 instead of target VLAN 10.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: On Switch1 interface Fa0/10, execute 'switchport access vlan 10'.

symptom: Trunk port between Switch1 and Switch2 is down, disabling inter-switch traffic.
ai_root_cause: Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) negotiation fails to establish a trunk because both Switch1 Gi0/2 and Switch2 Gi0/2 are set to 'dynamic auto' administrative mode. Since neither side actively initiates trunk negotiation, the operational mode defaults to 'static access'.
ai_evidence: Both Switch1 and Switch2 show 'Administrative Mode: dynamic auto' and 'Operational Mode: static access' on interface Gi0/2.
ai_fix_steps: Enter configuration mode on Switch1: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/2'; Set the interface mode to trunk: 'switchport mode trunk'; Enter configuration mode on Switch2: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/2'; Set the interface mode to trunk: 'switchport mode trunk'; Verify operational status on both switches: 'show interfaces Gi0/2 switchport'

symptom: PC-A experiences intermittent loss of connectivity and duplicate IP warnings.
ai_root_cause: IP address conflict / duplicate IP configuration on the local subnet. Both PC-A and PC-B are assigned the same IPv4 address (192.168.1.100) with different MAC addresses (0001.AAAA.1111 and 0002.BBBB.2222), causing ARP flapping and communication disruption.
ai_evidence: PC-A and PC-B both show 'IP Address: 192.168.1.100' and Router1 'show ip arp' contains duplicate entries for 192.168.1.100 with MACs 0001.AAAA.1111 and 0002.BBBB.2222
ai_fix_steps: Reconfigure PC-B with a unique, unassigned IP address in the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet (e.g., 192.168.1.101/24) or configure it to obtain an IP via DHCP; Clear ARP cache on Router1 using the privileged EXEC command: 'clear arp-cache'; Verify resolved ARP bindings using 'show ip arp'

symptom: PC-1 can reach local subnet hosts (10.0.1.0/24) but cannot reach remote servers (10.0.2.10).
ai_root_cause: Default gateway misconfiguration on PC-1. PC-1 is configured with default gateway 10.0.1.254, but Router1's connected interface GigabitEthernet0/0 is configured with IP address 10.0.1.1.
ai_evidence: PC-1 ipconfig shows 'Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 10.0.1.254' whereas Router1 show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/0 has IP 10.0.1.1
ai_fix_steps: On PC-1, open network configuration settings and update the Default Gateway to 10.0.1.1; Verify connectivity by executing 'ping 10.0.2.10' from PC-1

symptom: Host PC-3 (172.16.10.50) cannot ping Gateway 172.16.10.1.
ai_root_cause: Subnet mask mismatch on PC-3. PC-3 is configured with a /16 subnet mask (255.255.0.0), whereas the router interface GigabitEthernet0/0 is configured with a /24 subnet mask (255.255.255.0).
ai_evidence: PC-3 Subnet Mask is 255.255.0.0 while Router Gi0/0 Internet Address is 172.16.10.1/24 (255.255.255.0)
ai_fix_steps: Configure PC-3 IP settings to use Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0; Verify connectivity from PC-3 by executing: 'ping 172.16.10.1'

symptom: Hosts on LAN failover fail when primary router R1 goes down.
ai_root_cause: HSRP group number mismatch between routers. R1 is configured for HSRP group 1 while R2 is configured for HSRP group 2, causing both routers to act as Active routers in separate HSRP groups rather than forming an Active/Standby pair.
ai_evidence: R1 show standby brief shows 'Grp 1' in Active state, while R2 show standby brief shows 'Grp 2' in Active state with Standby 'unknown'
ai_fix_steps: Enter interface configuration mode on R2: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0'; Remove incorrect HSRP group 2 configuration: 'no standby 2 ip 192.168.1.1'; Configure matching HSRP group 1 with the virtual IP: 'standby 1 ip 192.168.1.1'; Verify standby state synchronization: 'show standby brief'

symptom: Branch office PCs receive APIPA IP addresses (169.254.x.x) and cannot access company network.
ai_root_cause: The Branch Router interface GigabitEthernet0/0 is missing the 'ip helper-address' configuration. As a result, DHCP broadcast discovery messages from local Branch PCs are not being relayed across the WAN to the central DHCP server at 10.1.1.100, causing PCs to fall back to APIPA (169.254.x.x) addresses.
ai_evidence: show running-config interface Gi0/0 lacks 'ip helper-address 10.1.1.100'
ai_fix_steps: Enter Branch Router configuration mode: 'configure terminal'; Access LAN interface: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0'; Configure DHCP relay agent: 'ip helper-address 10.1.1.100'; On Branch PCs, release and renew IP address: 'ipconfig /renew'

symptom: New PCs added to Sales department fail to obtain IP address from Router DHCP pool.
ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool 'SALES_POOL' on Router1 is completely exhausted with 100% utilization (all 254 available IP addresses are leased), leaving no available addresses for newly connected PCs.
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL reports 'Utilization mark (high/low) : 100 / 0' and 'Total leased addresses : 254' out of 254 total addresses
ai_fix_steps: Clear expired or stale DHCP bindings in privileged EXEC mode: 'clear ip dhcp binding *'; If additional capacity is permanently required, expand the network subnet size (e.g., /23) or configure a shorter lease time under 'ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL'; Verify address availability: 'show ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL'

symptom: Router interface IP conflicts with newly connected host PC.
ai_root_cause: Router interface IP (192.168.1.1) was not excluded from the DHCP pool allocation range.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Configure 'ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.10' on global router prompt.

symptom: PCs in VLAN 40 receive IP addresses in 192.168.20.0/24 range instead of 192.168.40.0/24.
ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool 'VLAN40' is misconfigured with the incorrect network subnet '192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0' instead of '192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0', causing DHCP clients in VLAN 40 to receive IP addresses in the 192.168.20.0/24 range.
ai_evidence: DHCP configuration shows 'ip dhcp pool VLAN40' with 'network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0' while interface Gi0/0.40 is assigned IP address '192.168.40.1/24'
ai_fix_steps: Enter global configuration mode on the Router: 'configure terminal'; Enter DHCP pool configuration mode: 'ip dhcp pool VLAN40'; Correct the network statement: 'network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0'; Verify DHCP pool configuration: 'show running-config | section dhcp'

symptom: PC can ping 8.8.8.8 directly, but browsing to www.cisco.com fails with domain name resolution error.
ai_root_cause: Host PC is configured with an incorrect or unreachable DNS server address (192.168.1.254) instead of the valid DNS server (10.0.0.53), causing DNS query timeouts and failure to resolve domain names.
ai_evidence: Host PC ipconfig /all shows 'DNS Servers . . . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.1.254' and nslookup reports 'Connection to 192.168.1.254 timed out -- no servers could be reached.'
ai_fix_steps: Reconfigure Host PC network adapter settings to set the DNS server address to 10.0.0.53; If DHCP is configured on Router1, update the DHCP pool with 'dns-server 10.0.0.53' under the DHCP pool configuration mode; Verify domain resolution on Host PC by executing 'nslookup www.cisco.com'

symptom: Pinging server by FQDN 'server1.company.local' succeeds, but pinging short name 'server1' fails.
ai_root_cause: Missing DNS domain suffix configuration on client host.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Configure DNS domain search suffix 'company.local' on host or router DHCP pool option.

symptom: DNS queries sent to corporate DNS server 172.16.50.2 time out across the router.
ai_root_cause: ACL only permits TCP port 53 for DNS, blocking standard UDP port 53 DNS queries.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Modify ACL DMZ_IN to permit UDP port 53 traffic: 'permit udp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 172.16.50.2 eq 53'.

symptom: PC-A (192.168.10.10) gets IP and ping gateway works, but cannot reach Server in VLAN 30 (10.0.30.50).
ai_root_cause: Rule check failure: Missing Route: 'show ip route' has no gateway of last resort and no static/dynamic route for destination network 10.0.30.0/24.
ai_evidence: Deterministic Check [Routing Table Check]: Missing Route: 'show ip route' has no gateway of last resort and no static/dynamic route for destination network 10.0.30.0/24.
ai_fix_steps: Add static route on Router1: 'ip route 10.0.30.0 255.255.255.0 172.16.12.2'.

symptom: OSPF neighbor adjacency between Router1 and Router2 stays in INIT/EXSTART state.
ai_root_cause: OSPF Hello and Dead interval timer mismatch between Router1 and Router2 on interface GigabitEthernet0/1 prevents normal neighbor adjacency formation.
ai_evidence: Router1 interface Gi0/1 is configured with 'Hello 10, Dead 40' whereas Router2 interface Gi0/1 is configured with 'Hello 30, Dead 120'
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router2 interface configuration: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/1'; Align OSPF timers with Router1: 'ip ospf hello-interval 10' and 'ip ospf dead-interval 40'; Verify neighbor adjacency state reaches FULL: 'show ip ospf neighbor'

symptom: Router2 does not form EIGRP neighbor relationship with Router1.
ai_root_cause: Autonomous System (AS) number mismatch between routers. Router1 is configured with EIGRP AS 100, whereas Router2 is configured with EIGRP AS 200. EIGRP routers must be in the same Autonomous System to establish adjacency.
ai_evidence: Router1 shows 'EIGRP-IPv4 Interfaces for AS(100)' while Router2 configuration contains 'router eigrp 200'
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router2 global configuration mode: 'configure terminal'; Remove incorrect EIGRP AS process: 'no router eigrp 200'; Configure matching EIGRP AS process: 'router eigrp 100'; Add network statement: 'network 172.16.1.0 0.0.0.3'; Verify adjacency: 'show ip eigrp neighbors'

symptom: Router1 fails to advertise LAN routes to Router2 via OSPF.
ai_root_cause: GigabitEthernet0/1 is incorrectly configured as a passive-interface under OSPF process 1 on Router1. This suppresses OSPF Hello packets on the link to Router2, preventing neighbor adjacency from forming and stopping route advertisements.
ai_evidence: router ospf 1 contains 'passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/1' and show ip ospf neighbor reports '(No active OSPF neighbors on Gi0/1)'
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router1 global configuration mode: 'configure terminal'; Enter OSPF router configuration: 'router ospf 1'; Remove passive interface on Gi0/1: 'no passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/1'; Optionally make LAN interface Gi0/0 passive instead if intended: 'passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0'; Verify OSPF adjacency state: 'show ip ospf neighbor'

symptom: BGP session between HQ Router (AS 65001) and ISP Router (AS 65500) fails to establish.
ai_root_cause: Autonomous System (AS) number mismatch on HQ Router. HQ Router is configured to peer with neighbor 203.0.113.2 using remote AS 65501, but the ISP Router is operating in AS 65500.
ai_evidence: HQ Router 'show ip bgp summary' shows neighbor 203.0.113.2 configured with AS 65501 in Active state, while ISP Router configuration specifies 'router bgp 65500'.
ai_fix_steps: Enter HQ Router BGP configuration mode: 'router bgp 65001'; Remove the incorrect neighbor AS definition: 'no neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote-as 65501'; Configure the correct remote AS for the ISP neighbor: 'neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote-as 65500'; Verify BGP session establishment: 'show ip bgp summary'

symptom: PC-A (192.168.10.5) cannot access Web Server (10.0.0.100) on port 80.
ai_root_cause: Extended access list BLOCK_WEB applied outbound on Router1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 explicitly denies TCP port 80 traffic from PC-A (192.168.10.5) to the Web Server (10.0.0.100).
ai_evidence: show ip access-lists BLOCK_WEB shows '10 deny tcp host 192.168.10.5 host 10.0.0.100 eq 80' and show ip interface Gi0/1 shows 'Outbound access list is BLOCK_WEB'
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router1 configuration mode for the ACL: 'ip access-list extended BLOCK_WEB'; Remove the deny rule: 'no 10'; Optionally permit required traffic: 'permit ip any any'; Alternatively remove the ACL from the interface: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/1' followed by 'no ip access-group BLOCK_WEB out'; Verify configuration: 'show ip access-lists BLOCK_WEB'

symptom: Host 192.168.1.50 can still SSH to Server 10.0.0.5 despite access list blocking rule.
ai_root_cause: ACL rule checks port 23 (Telnet) instead of port 22 (SSH).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Replace rule 10 in SEC_ACL with 'deny tcp host 192.168.1.50 host 10.0.0.5 eq 22'.

symptom: Entire HR department (192.168.20.0/24) is blocked from accessing Internet.
ai_root_cause: Wildcard mask 0.0.0.255 matches the entire /24 subnet instead of host 192.168.20.5 (host / 0.0.0.0).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Update ACL 10 rule 10 to 'deny host 192.168.20.5' or 'deny 192.168.20.5 0.0.0.0'.

symptom: Inter-departmental traffic between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 drops at router interface.
ai_root_cause: ACL missing permit statement at end, dropping all traffic coming into Gi0/0.10.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Add 'permit ip any any' to FILTER_VLAN10.

symptom: Internal LAN PCs (192.168.1.0/24) cannot reach external Internet IP addresses (8.8.8.8).
ai_root_cause: Missing 'ip nat inside' on Gi0/0 and 'ip nat outside' on Gi0/1 interface configurations.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Apply 'ip nat inside' on interface Gi0/0 and 'ip nat outside' on interface Gi0/1.

symptom: LAN subnet 192.168.2.0/24 hosts cannot access Internet via NAT, while 192.168.1.0/24 works.
ai_root_cause: NAT ACL 10 does not permit the newly added subnet 192.168.2.0/24.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Add line 'access-list 10 permit 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255' to global configuration.

symptom: External clients cannot reach internal Web Server via Static NAT IP 203.0.113.50.
ai_root_cause: Static NAT translation maps public IP to wrong internal IP (192.168.1.55 instead of 192.168.1.50).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Correct static NAT entry to 'ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.50 203.0.113.50'.

symptom: Wireless Laptop cannot connect to Access Point; authentication fails continuously.
ai_root_cause: WPA2 Pre-Shared Key mismatch between laptop ('SecretPass123') and Access Point ('SecretPass123!').
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Update laptop wireless security key to match AP key 'SecretPass123!'.

symptom: Wireless clients see SSID 'Staff_WiFi' but fail to obtain an IP address via DHCP.
ai_root_cause: Rule check failure: VLAN 50 is missing from the switch VLAN database.
ai_evidence: Deterministic Check [VLAN Database Check]: VLAN 50 is missing from the switch VLAN database.
ai_fix_steps: Add VLAN 50 to Switch1 VLAN database and trunk allowed list.

symptom: Lightweight Access Point (LAP-1) remains in joining loop and fails to discover WLC.
ai_root_cause: DHCP pool AP_POOL missing Option 43 (hex value for WLC IP 10.10.10.5).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Add 'option 43 hex f1040a0a0a05' to DHCP pool AP_POOL.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users can ping internal corporate server 10.0.0.100.
ai_root_cause: Guest VLAN 99 interface lacks access group blocking traffic to internal subnets (10.0.0.0/8).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Apply inbound ACL on Gi0/0.99 blocking 10.0.0.0/8 destination traffic.

symptom: PC in VLAN 10 cannot access Web Server in VLAN 20. Neither VLAN can reach Internet.
ai_root_cause: Router interface Gi0/0 missing subinterface VLAN encapsulation (Gi0/0.10 & Gi0/0.20) and missing default static route.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Configure subinterfaces Gi0/0.10 and Gi0/0.20 with dot1q encapsulation and default route 'ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.2'.

symptom: PC receives IP via DHCP but cannot resolve domain names or ping outside subnet.
ai_root_cause: DHCP pool specifies invalid gateway and DNS server IP (192.168.1.254 instead of router IP 192.168.1.1).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Update DHCP pool config: default-router 192.168.1.1, dns-server 8.8.8.8.

symptom: Finance PC-1 (10.10.10.15) ping to Accounting Server (10.20.20.50) fails intermittently.
ai_root_cause: Rule check failure: Interface status error: Port security violation triggered err-disabled / Secure-shutdown state.
ai_evidence: Deterministic Check [Interface Status Check]: Interface status error: Port security violation triggered err-disabled / Secure-shutdown state.
ai_fix_steps: Clear port violation with 'shutdown' / 'no shutdown' on Fa0/1 after authorizing MAC address.
